newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary forex futures trade eyes longer term.
newsitem.headline: Hungary forex futures trade eyes longer term.

text.p: The Hungarian currency futures market saw quiet trade on Monday as traders continued to look forward for trends, with December 1997 taking most attention.
The Budapest Commodities Exchange (BCE) recorded a modest 3.05 billion forints turnover, while the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) saw no trade and no price changes.
On the BCE the mark, dollar, yen and Swiss franc all saw significant turnover, with December 1997 the most traded contract, for which most prices moved slightly downwards. @
"We don't expect a further weakening on the spot market of the forint against the basket in the near future," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle.
"December yen and Swiss franc are still attractive because of their low interest rates relative to the forint's future devaluation," he said.
On Monday's forex spot market the Hungarian unit moved closer to the resistance level (bid) of the central bank's 4.5 percent intervention band, ending 35 pips from the bid at 175.75 to the dollar.
For December maturity the yen fell 25 fillers to 167.15 forints per 100 yen, the Swiss franc dropped eight fillers to 135.30 and the dollar fell 10 fillers to 194.10 forints.
The December mark rose five fillers to 116.80 forints.
